analysis:
Both changed files are CI test scripts (scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py, scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py). They add assertions that pin workflow properties; no runtime provider, coordinator, or attestation code changed. The affected threat-model entries are only tangential: TB-011 and T-054 cover build qualification and the signed artifact path, and T-041 covers the cache.

Security-relevant properties the tests now assert:
- Only pushes to master/dev save caches (SAVE_CACHES env, `inputs.save-caches` in the composite action), so PR-controlled code cannot poison caches that later branches restore. Tests at ~lines 785-805 pin `if:` on every cache/save step and require save-caches to be passed by all 5 build-action callers.
- Checkouts use `persist-credentials: false`, so a token is not written to .git/config and then saved in the .git cache. Tests at ~lines 840-860 check the options of both the cached and cold checkout.
- Exactly one checkout step per job may use continue-on-error (the cached attempt). The cold fallback runs only on failure and fails the job. `without_cached_checkout` makes the no-continue-on-error assertions exclude only that step.
- The workflow has no secrets, environment, id-token, or repository inputs, and runs no backend execution (tests at lines 241-256 of test-ci-component-paths.py).
- The provider-test-gate truth table is retained: skipped lanes pass only when the classifier did not select them.
- Cache keys are bound to the runner layout and lane (SwiftPM repos).

Remaining unverified contract: the actual ci.yml and action.yml are not in this batch, so I could not confirm that they match what the tests assert. One residual cache-trust question is that a restored .git cache saved by master pushes is reused by PR jobs. That is acceptable because PRs never save, and the cold fallback exists. The sparse-checkout test only verifies git behavior locally. No regression was identified in the supplied test code.
